test_title: PYST 20 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 19 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

He said, "The train will leave in ten minutes."

options.text: He said that the train would leave in ten minutes.
He said that the train will leave in ten minutes.
He said that the train left in ten minutes.
He said that the train was leaving in ten minutes.

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "The train will leave in ten minutes."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"said"** remains **"said"** in indirect speech because it is not followed by an object (e.g., "said to me").
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The comma and quotation marks are removed and replaced by the conjunction **"that"** to connect the reporting clause with the reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Will to Would):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the future tense modal **"will"** must be changed to its past equivalent, **"would"**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** The sentence follows the standard rule for assertive sentences where the tense shifts backward when the reporting verb is in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said that the train would leave in ten minutes."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said that the train will leave in ten minutes." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the modal "will" to "would," which is necessary when the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said that the train left in ten minutes." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "will leave" (future) is incorrectly changed to "left" (simple past), which alters the original meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said that the train was leaving in ten minutes." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the tense to past continuous, which does not accurately reflect the simple future "will leave."
